name: Bharti Airtel Ltd
title: Bharti Airtel Ltd - 532454 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Telco is supply-disciplined but ARPU stalled: Q4 ARPU Rs.257 up only Rs.3 QoQ, management "not happy", with radio capex moderating and FY27 capex guided "in the ballpark" of FY26's ~Rs.31,000 Cr.

summary.headline: Airtel FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record ~Rs 2,11,000 Cr; Q4 India ARPU rose only Rs 3 to Rs 257 on EDB basis.
summary.overview: Management reported a record FY26 with consolidated revenue of about Rs 2,11,000 Cr and EBITDAaL of about Rs 1,08,000 Cr (51.2% margin). Q4 consolidated revenue was about Rs 55,400 Cr, up 2.6% QoQ, with Q4 constant currency growth of 1.1% hit by seasonality and fewer days. India mobile ARPU rose only Rs 3 QoQ on an EDB basis, which management said it was not happy with, citing West Asia-linked international roaming and handset price pressures. The Board recommended a dividend of Rs 24 per share (vs Rs 16) and approved a no-cash share swap with ICIL to acquire an additional 16.3% of Airtel Africa. Management flagged geopolitical cost pressures on capex, energy, roaming and servers/memory, and pivoted home broadband back to fiber from FWA.

financial_highlights.metric: Airtel Payments Bank annualised revenue run rate

segments.name: India mobile
segments.commentary: Q4 added 4.7 mn customers (5.8 mn smartphone adds in the quarter per the call); ARPU Rs 257, up Rs 3 on EDB basis. Mobile is about 52% of revenue.

segments.name: Homes (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 net adds 1.1 mn; added 4.2 mn customers in FY26 and crossed 45 mn home passes after ~8 mn passes rolled out in FY26. Digital TV added nearly 0.5 mn customers in Q4 on IPTV.

segments.name: Airtel Business (B2B)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about Rs 5,500 Cr, +2.6% QoQ; order book grew 17% in FY26; digital businesses revenue +27% in FY26. Non-mobile India is 13% of revenue.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Africa is 29% of group revenue; Q4 constant currency growth 1.1%, affected by seasonality and fewer days.

segments.name: Financial services / Airtel Money
segments.commentary: Airtel Money received RBI approval to operate as an NBFC; monthly loan disbursement run rate over Rs 550 Cr; Payments Bank has ~120 mn monthly transacting users and deposits over Rs 4,600 Cr (+27% YoY).

segments.name: Bharti Hexacom
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue +9.4%, EBITDAaL +17.9%, margin 47.6% (+3.4 pts); record net homes adds of 395,000 in FY26; Q4 mobile net adds about 370,000, 28.8 mn base, ARPU Rs 252 (EDB ~Rs 257-258).

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; FY27 capex expected to be 'in the ballpark' of FY26 (~Rs 31,000 Cr India excl. passive), give or take a little.
Radio capex in India is moderating; transport capex to be increased; 56 edge data centers to be built over 18-24 months.
Dividend policy progressive; Board sees further buybacks possible in coming years to help BTL move toward 51% stake.
Africa share swap with ICIL (no cash, 16.3% additional stake in Airtel Africa) to take Airtel's Africa stake to about 78%, with ambition to go towards 90%.
Airtel Money NBFC: Rs 20,000 Cr over five years cited for financial services, of which Rs 14,000 Cr from Airtel, though management said actual spend likely much less.
Management expects some B2B margin pressure as cloud, CPaaS and digital businesses grow at lower margins than connectivity.
capex_capacity: India capex excl. passive FY26 about Rs 31,000 Cr; FY27 expected in similar ballpark. Wireless capex ~16% of sales (derived, per analyst), described as a decade low.

Nxtra targets 1 GW data center capacity over the next few years; Nxtra $1 bn fundraise announced; colocation model, including a build for Google's AI data center in Visakhapatnam; no GPU-as-a-service at present.
Airtel Cloud: 24-25 deals secured by year end, with further wins in April; three cloud regions currently.
Homes: FTTH home-pass expansion accelerated; ~43,000 km of fiber rolled out in FY26; ~7,800 network sites added; 42,000 sites with solar access.
Hexacom Q4 capex Rs 586 Cr, directed to 5G densification, network modernisation and homes/IPTV.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian pricing architecture is broken: unlimited data plans cap out at ~Rs 340-350; Rs 199 entry pack price left unchanged for now; a tiered small/medium/large/extra-large structure proposed as path to ARPU growth, without a timeline.
ARPU headwinds in Q4: lower international roaming (West Asia), handset price increases affecting 2G-4G upgrades, and 5G pack adoption; management said no red flags on ARPU.
Handset shipments softened and prices rose sharply in recent weeks; not yet impacting but being watched.
Homes: new-add ARPU not declining, blended ARPU dilution from mix; quarter-on-quarter ARPU bottoming in last two quarters.
B2B: messaging flat to slightly declining (price pressure, OTT shift); connectivity grows at low single digits industry-wide with Airtel gaining share; digital businesses carry lower margins.
FWA: chipset/memory price spikes over last 3-4 months made FWA costlier than fiber; pivot to fiber-first from April, with FWA kept for hard-to-reach areas, especially at Hexacom.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be allocated given strong India FCF and the dividend payout level, and are non-India acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities are core business first, then deleveraging, then adjacencies (data centers, financial services, cloud). Management said nothing further outside India is planned for now beyond bolt-ons in towers, cloud, cybersecurity and B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Does ARPU growth need tariff hikes, and what will change the trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued pricing architecture must be fixed rather than just raising entry prices, which it said must be done with caution. Levers cited: postpaid, best-fit plan upgrades, roaming and data-consumption upgrades.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 ARPU expansion slow given roaming and handset headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashwat said organic levers (postpaid, plan upgrades within tiers) provide headroom for many quarters, but handset price rises need watching.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for the coming year and capital allocation shift toward growth bets?
qa_highlights.answer: Radio capex moderating in India; transport, edge data centers, homes, data centers and cloud to get focus. FY27 capex expected roughly in line with FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE targets and Nxtra's business model, including Google partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give ROCE targets; consolidated ROCE ~19%, expected to improve with operating leverage. Nxtra is colocation-led, with Google's Visakhapatnam AI data center being built as colocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is wireless capex near the bottom, and what is the homes ARPU trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Wireless capex is derived at ~16% of sales and is moderating; 5G densification would be done if needed. Homes ARPU dilution is from mix; acquisition ARPU stable, and quarterly ARPU is bottoming.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 ARPU lag and what is the regulatory charge at Hexacom?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower roaming, handset price rises and 5G pack adoption were the drivers. The regulatory charge was a prudential provision from a changed interpretation of an existing matter, not new demand.

risks_watch: Handset shipments softening and sharp handset price rises in recent weeks could slow feature-phone to smartphone upgrades and weigh on India ARPU in FY27; management said it has not yet seen impact but cannot rule it out.
Geopolitical cost pressures: INR depreciation on capex, energy price increases, restricted gas supply hitting galvanising and tower build-outs, and servers/memory price spikes.

Homes: FWA costlier than fiber after chipset/memory price spikes over the last 3-4 months; pivot to fiber-first from April, with the shift expected to ramp over the next couple of months, so home net adds pace is a watch item.
International roaming (West Asia) headwind on ARPU, with management saying it will see how roaming plays out this year; 5G pack adoption also diluting ARPU.

Finance cost stickiness (~Rs 4,000 Cr) and the Africa share swap with ICIL; management expects reduction going forward but gave no figures. Airtel Money NBFC launch, with Rs 20,000 Cr five-year plan cited and collections/delinquency discipline flagged as critical.
B2B margin pressure as cloud, CPaaS and digital businesses grow at lower margins than connectivity; order book +17% in FY26 but no FY27 growth figure given.
key_quotes: Fundamentally, my belief is that the price architecture in this country is broken.
So we have pivoted the whole company back to a dramatic obsession on fiber.
The fixed wireless access has now become very much more expensive.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core India franchise, FCF, dividend and Africa stake increase, but openly unhappy with the Rs 3 QoQ ARPU gain and candid about handset and roaming headwinds. Evasive on tariff hikes (pricing architecture "broken", but no timeline or Rs 199 change), on ROCE targets, and on Hexacom's lag versus Airtel; no formal guidance given.

adds.what: Nxtra 1 GW data centre capacity target over next few years (colocation model)
56 edge data centres to be built over 18-24 months
~43,000 km fiber rolled out in FY26 and ~8 mn home passes added (FTTH expansion accelerated)

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; FY27 India capex guided 'in the ballpark' of ~Rs 31,000 Cr, backed by fiber home-pass rollout, 7,800 new sites, Nxtra 1 GW plan and Airtel Business order book up 17% in FY26, while Q4 constant-currency growth was only 1.1% and India ARPU rose just Rs 3.
